/* Shared, dependency-free fold controller for Workflow and Dataset pages. */
(function (global) {
  "use strict";

  var SELECTOR = "section.fold";
  var ready = false;

  function sections() {
    return Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll(SELECTOR)).filter(function (section) { return !section.hidden; });
  }

  function parts(section) {
    if (!section) return {};
    var head = section.querySelector(":scope > h2 > button.fold-head");
    var body = head && document.getElementById(head.getAttribute("aria-controls"));
    return { head: head, body: body };
  }

  function isOpen(section) {
    var body = parts(section).body;
    return !!body && !body.hasAttribute("data-folded");
  }

  function announce(section, open) {
    section.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(open ? "fold:open" : "fold:close", {
      bubbles: true, detail: { section: section }
    }));
  }

  function setOpen(section, open, opts) {
    var pair = parts(section);
    if (section.hidden || !pair.head || !pair.body) return false;
    var changed = isOpen(section) !== open;
    pair.body.toggleAttribute("data-folded", !open);
    pair.head.setAttribute("aria-expanded", open ? "true" : "false");
    if (changed || (opts && opts.forceEvent)) announce(section, open);
    return true;
  }

  function targetForHash() {
    var id;
    try { id = decodeURIComponent(global.location.hash.slice(1)); }
    catch (_) { return null; }
    if (!id) return null;
    var target = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!target) return null;
    var section = target.matches && target.matches(SELECTOR) ? target : target.closest(SELECTOR);
    return section && !section.hidden ? { section: section, target: target } : null;
  }

  function openId(id, scroll) {
    var target = document.getElementById(id);
    if (!target) return false;
    var section = target.matches && target.matches(SELECTOR) ? target : target.closest(SELECTOR);
    if (!section || section.hidden) return false;
    setOpen(section, true, { forceEvent: true });
    if (scroll && target.scrollIntoView) target.scrollIntoView({ block: "start" });
    return true;
  }

  function setAll(open) {
    sections().forEach(function (section) { setOpen(section, open, { forceEvent: open }); });
    document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("folds:set-all", { detail: { open: open } }));
  }

  function openHash(scroll) {
    var found = targetForHash();
    if (!found) return false;
    setOpen(found.section, true, { forceEvent: true });
    if (scroll && found.target.scrollIntoView) found.target.scrollIntoView({ block: "start" });
    return true;
  }

  function moveFocus(head, key) {
    var heads = sections().map(function (section) { return parts(section).head; }).filter(Boolean);
    var at = heads.indexOf(head);
    if (at < 0) return;
    var next = key === "Home" ? 0 : key === "End" ? heads.length - 1 :
      key === "ArrowDown" ? (at + 1) % heads.length : (at - 1 + heads.length) % heads.length;
    heads[next].focus();
  }

  function bind() {
    if (!ready) {
      document.documentElement.classList.add("pc-folds-ready");
      ready = true;
    }
    sections().forEach(function (section) {
      var pair = parts(section);
      if (!pair.head || !pair.body || pair.head.dataset.foldBound) return;
      pair.head.dataset.foldBound = "true";
      pair.body.removeAttribute("hidden");
      setOpen(section, false);
      pair.head.addEventListener("click", function () { setOpen(section, !isOpen(section)); });
      pair.head.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
        if (["ArrowUp", "ArrowDown", "Home", "End"].indexOf(event.key) < 0) return;
        event.preventDefault();
        moveFocus(pair.head, event.key);
      });
    });

    document.querySelectorAll(".fold-controls [data-fold-action]").forEach(function (button) {
      if (button.dataset.foldBound) return;
      button.dataset.foldBound = "true";
      button.addEventListener("click", function () {
        if (button.dataset.foldAction === "open-all") setAll(true);
        if (button.dataset.foldAction === "close-all") setAll(false);
      });
    });

    document.querySelectorAll("[data-fold-target]").forEach(function (control) {
      if (control.dataset.foldTargetBound) return;
      control.dataset.foldTargetBound = "true";
      control.addEventListener("click", function () {
        var id = control.dataset.foldTarget;
        if (openId(id, true) && global.location.hash !== "#" + id) {
          global.history.replaceState(null, "", "#" + encodeURIComponent(id));
        }
      });
      control.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
        if (event.key !== "Enter" && event.key !== " ") return;
        event.preventDefault(); control.click();
      });
    });

    openHash(false);
  }

  global.PCFolds = {
    bind: bind, isOpen: isOpen, setOpen: setOpen, open: openId,
    setAll: setAll, sections: sections
  };
  if (document.readyState === "loading") document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", bind);
  else bind();
  global.addEventListener("hashchange", function () { openHash(true); });
}(window));

/* Shared runtime for both folded page skeletons. It parses the one payload,
   coalesces repaint scopes, and owns theme/fold/resize repaint wiring. */
"use strict";
const D = JSON.parse(document.getElementById("payload").textContent);
(function (global) {
  const PC = global.PC = global.PC || {};

  /* Page-owned theme lifecycle: URL preference, control, system changes and
     external data-theme changes share one coalesced repaint path. */
  PC.initTheme = function (opts) {
    opts = typeof opts === "function" ? { redraw: opts } : (opts || {});
    const redraw = typeof opts.redraw === "function" ? opts.redraw : function () {};
    let queued = false;
    function fire() {
      if (queued) return;
      queued = true;
      (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (fn) { return setTimeout(fn, 16); })(function () {
        queued = false;
        if (PC.repaintThemePainters) PC.repaintThemePainters();
        redraw();
      });
    }
    const param = opts.param || "theme";
    let query = null;
    try { query = new URLSearchParams(global.location.search).get(param); } catch (_) {}
    if (query === "dark" || query === "light") PC.setTheme(query);
    const button = opts.button
      ? (typeof opts.button === "string" ? document.querySelector(opts.button) : opts.button)
      : document.getElementById(opts.buttonId || "themeBtn");
    function labelButton() {
      if (button) button.setAttribute("aria-label", "Switch to " +
        (PC.isDark() ? "light" : "dark") + " theme");
    }
    if (button && !button.dataset.pcThemeBound) {
      button.dataset.pcThemeBound = "true";
      button.addEventListener("click", function () {
        PC.setTheme(PC.isDark() ? "light" : "dark"); labelButton(); fire();
      });
    }
    labelButton();
    const mq = global.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
    const systemChanged = function () { labelButton(); fire(); };
    if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener("change", systemChanged);
    else if (mq.addListener) mq.addListener(systemChanged);
    if (global.MutationObserver) {
      new MutationObserver(function () { labelButton(); fire(); })
        .observe(document.documentElement,
                 { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["data-theme"] });
    }
    return {
      redraw: fire,
      set: function (theme) { PC.setTheme(theme); labelButton(); fire(); },
      toggle: function () { PC.setTheme(PC.isDark() ? "light" : "dark"); labelButton(); fire(); },
      isDark: PC.isDark
    };
  };

  const painters = [];
  const reasons = new Set();
  let frame = 0;
  let dirtyScope = null;

  PC.registerRepaint = function (paint) {
    if (typeof paint !== "function") throw new TypeError("registerRepaint expects a function");
    if (!painters.includes(paint)) painters.push(paint);
    return function () {
      const at = painters.indexOf(paint);
      if (at >= 0) painters.splice(at, 1);
    };
  };

  /* A document request dominates. Two different scoped requests promote to
     document so no fold opened in the same frame loses its paint. */
  PC.repaint = function (reason, scope) {
    const next = scope && typeof scope.querySelectorAll === "function" ? scope : document;
    reasons.add(reason || "manual");
    if (dirtyScope === document || next === document) dirtyScope = document;
    else if (dirtyScope === null || dirtyScope === next) dirtyScope = next;
    else dirtyScope = document;
    if (frame) return;
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(function () {
      const event = { reason: Array.from(reasons).join("+"), scope: dirtyScope || document };
      frame = 0; dirtyScope = null; reasons.clear();
      painters.slice().forEach(function (paint) { paint(event); });
      document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("pc:repaint", { detail: event }));
    });
  };

  document.addEventListener("fold:open", function (event) {
    PC.repaint("fold-open", event.target);
  });
  document.addEventListener("folds:set-all", function (event) {
    if (event.detail && event.detail.open) PC.repaint("open-all", document);
    else if (PC.hideTip) PC.hideTip();
  });
  global.addEventListener("resize", PC.debounce(function () {
    PC.repaint("resize", document);
  }, 120));
  PC.initTheme({ redraw: function () { PC.repaint("theme", document); } });
}(window));

/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   PHONE FOLD + TAB SCROLL POLICY  —  page behaviour module
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Owner review of real phone screenshots: on a handset the story strip and the
   header workflow figure each consume about a full screen before any content
   is reachable, and tapping a tab threw the reader back to the top of the
   page. This module fixes all three without changing either component renderer: it runs
   after PC has rendered and adapts the DOM it finds, so a demo inherits the
   behaviour by rebuilding and no template changes.

   WHY A SEPARATE IIFE. renderStory/renderDag are load-bearing and gated
   (check_design 13 asserts the published DAG geometry). Wrapping their output
   from outside cannot change what they draw or what they publish — it only
   changes whether the finished figure is open on a narrow screen.

   THE FIGURES STAY FIGURES (DESIGN.md §2.4, §3.2). Both sections forbid a
   <button>, an href, a click handler or a focus ring INSIDE the figure. So the
   disclosure is never placed inside: a native <details> is inserted AROUND the
   figure and the figure is moved into it untouched. .storystrip / .dagfig keep
   role="figure", keep their aria-label and still contain no control. The
   <summary> is page furniture wrapping the figure, which is exactly what §2.4
   allows — it is not a panel, not a stage and not a "current" marker.

   DESKTOP IS BYTE-IDENTICAL IN BEHAVIOUR. Above the phone breakpoint the
   <details> is forced open and components.css hides the <summary>, so the
   rendered page is what it always was. The fold state follows the viewport
   until the reader touches it, after which their choice is kept for the rest
   of the session (folds carry data-pc-user once toggled by hand).
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
(function (global) {
  "use strict";
  var doc = global.document;
  if (!doc) return;

  var PHONE = "(max-width: 640px)";
  function isPhone() {
    try { return global.matchMedia(PHONE).matches; } catch (e) { return false; }
  }

  /* The natural document Y of an element. offsetTop walks the layout tree and
     is NOT moved by position:sticky (sticky is a paint-time offset), which is
     the whole reason it is used here: the tab strip is sticky at top:0, so its
     getBoundingClientRect().top reads 0 whenever it is stuck and cannot tell us
     where the strip actually lives in the document. */
  function docTop(el) {
    var y = 0;
    while (el) { y += el.offsetTop || 0; el = el.offsetParent; }
    return y;
  }

  /* ── 1 + 2 · fold the story strip and the workflow figure on a phone ─────── */

  function repaintInside(el) {
    var PC = global.PC;
    if (!PC) return;
    try { if (el.querySelector(".dagfig, .dagcols") || el.classList.contains("dagfig")) PC.repaintDags(); } catch (e) {}
    try { if (el.querySelector(".storystrip") || el.classList.contains("storystrip")) PC.repaintStories(); } catch (e) {}
  }

  function fold(fig, summaryText) {
    if (!fig || !fig.parentNode) return null;
    if (fig.closest && fig.closest("details.pcfold")) return null;   // already folded
    if (fig.hidden) return null;                                     // no story block: leave hidden

    var det = doc.createElement("details");
    det.className = "pcfold";
    var sum = doc.createElement("summary");
    sum.className = "pcfoldsum";
    sum.textContent = summaryText || "Show";
    fig.parentNode.insertBefore(det, fig);
    det.appendChild(sum);
    det.appendChild(fig);                       // the figure moves in UNCHANGED

    /* A canvas measured while its <details> is closed has a zero CSS box, so
       every thumbnail and every DAG edge is redrawn the moment it opens. */
    det.addEventListener("toggle", function () {
      if (det.open) {
        (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(function () {
          repaintInside(det);
        });
      }
    });
    /* A hand toggle pins the state: after this the viewport no longer decides
       for the reader. */
    sum.addEventListener("click", function () { det.dataset.pcUser = "1"; });
    return det;
  }

  function syncFolds() {
    var phone = isPhone();
    var list = doc.querySelectorAll("details.pcfold");
    for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
      var det = list[i];
      if (det.dataset.pcUser === "1") continue;      // the reader has decided
      var want = !phone;                             // open everywhere except a phone
      if (det.open !== want) {
        det.open = want;
        if (want) repaintInside(det);
      }
    }
  }

  function storySummary() {
    /* The headline question IS the summary: collapsed, a phone still shows the
       one line §2.4 calls the whole point of the strip. */
    var q = doc.querySelector(".storystrip .storyq");
    var text = q && q.textContent ? q.textContent.trim() : "";
    return text || "What this demo is about";
  }

  function dagSummary() {
    var steps = doc.querySelectorAll(".dagfig .dagnode").length;
    if (steps) return "Analysis workflow — 4 stages · " + steps + " steps";
    var segs = doc.querySelectorAll(".ribbon .rseg").length;
    if (segs) return "Analysis workflow — " + segs + " stages";
    return "Analysis workflow";
  }

  function installFolds() {
    var story = doc.querySelector(".storystrip");
    if (story) fold(story, storySummary());

    /* The DAG host when the page has a card, else the bare rollup a legacy
       page ships. Never both: .dagroll lives INSIDE .dagfig. */
    var wf = doc.querySelector(".dagfig");
    if (!wf) {
      var ribbons = doc.querySelectorAll(".ribbon");
      for (var i = 0; i < ribbons.length; i++) {
        if (!ribbons[i].closest(".dagfig")) { wf = ribbons[i]; break; }
      }
    }
    if (wf) fold(wf, dagSummary());

    syncFolds();
  }

  /* ── 3b · a tab must not throw the reader back to the top of the page ─────
     Every demo template carries its own PC.selectTop, and six of them end it
     with scrollTo({top:0}) — which on a phone means the reader lands back above
     the masthead, the story strip and the workflow figure every single time
     they change tab. The templates cannot all be edited from here, so the
     policy is applied from the shared library instead: this listener runs on
     document in the BUBBLE phase, i.e. after the chip's own handler has
     already scrolled, and puts the viewport back at the tab strip.

     The correction is queued in rAF, which runs before the next paint, so the
     intermediate scroll to 0 is never rendered — the reader sees no jump.
     Phone only: on a desktop the existing scroll-to-top is the documented
     behaviour and is left alone. */
  function tabScrollPolicy(evt) {
    if (!isPhone()) return;
    var t = evt.target;
    if (!t || !t.closest) return;
    var chip = t.closest('.toptabs [role="tab"], .toptabs .tab');
    if (!chip) return;
    var strip = chip.closest(".toptabs");
    if (!strip) return;
    var y = docTop(strip);
    (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(function () {
      if (Math.abs((global.scrollY || 0) - y) > 1) {
        try { global.scrollTo({ top: y, behavior: "auto" }); }
        catch (e) { global.scrollTo(0, y); }
      }
    });
  }

  function boot() {
    installFolds();
    doc.addEventListener("click", tabScrollPolicy, false);
    try {
      var mq = global.matchMedia(PHONE);
      if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener("change", syncFolds);
      else if (mq.addListener) mq.addListener(syncFolds);
    } catch (e) {}
    global.addEventListener("resize", function () { syncFolds(); });
  }

  /* The page script renders the story strip and the DAG during its own load
     handler, so the fold is installed after that: DOM ready, then one more
     turn. installFolds is idempotent, so running it twice is harmless and the
     second pass catches a figure rendered late. */
  function schedule() {
    boot();
    setTimeout(installFolds, 0);
    global.addEventListener("load", function () { setTimeout(installFolds, 0); });
  }
  if (doc.readyState === "loading") doc.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", schedule);
  else schedule();

  if (global.PC) {
    global.PC.syncFolds = syncFolds;
    global.PC.installFolds = installFolds;
  }
})(typeof globalThis !== "undefined" ? globalThis : this);

/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   PHONE PARAMETER BAR  —  page behaviour module
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Owner review on a REAL handset: on tab 3 the .filters control panel is most
   of a phone screen tall, so the controls and the plots they drive are never
   visible together. You change the embedding, then scroll to find out what it
   did. On a laptop the two are side by side and nothing is wrong.

   On a phone this collapses each .filters panel behind a slim sticky bar
   carrying a LIVE SUMMARY of the panel's current values — "t-SNE · perplexity
   30 · k 6" — pinned directly under the sticky tab strip. Tap the bar and the
   full panel pushes down under it; change any control and the summary updates
   and the panel collapses again, so the plot is on screen the moment the value
   changes. Tap the bar again to reopen: the return trip is always one tap.

   GENERIC BY CONSTRUCTION. The bar and the summary are derived from the
   panel's OWN markup — the .fgroup label text and the live control values —
   so every demo with a .filters panel inherits this by rebuilding, and no
   template is edited. Nothing here is demo-specific.

   WHY A SEPARATE IIFE, AND WHY IT IS SAFE FOR THE GATE. It only rearranges
   chrome around an existing panel. Critically, collapsing uses display:none on
   the PANEL while every control stays in the DOM: the design acceptance
   pass (§9.3) drives controls purely in JS — `el.selectedIndex = …; fire(el,
   "change")`, `el.click()` — never by coordinate and never checking
   visibility, so a collapsed panel is still fully exercised at 380x844.

   SPEC. DESIGN.md §6.3 calls .filters a "sticky control bar … positioned below
   the sticky tabs" and §5.2 fixes the offset at `top: topTabs.offsetHeight` —
   which is exactly what this restores on phones, at 44px instead of a full
   panel. The bar is a CONTROL SURFACE, not navigation: one <button
   aria-expanded aria-controls>, no role="navigation", no aria-current, no
   stage colour. The selects inside stay native (§6.3). Flat — the only shadow
   in the suite is #tip (§6.1).
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
(function (global) {
  "use strict";
  var doc = global.document;
  if (!doc) return;

  var PHONE = "(max-width: 640px)";
  function isPhone() {
    try { return global.matchMedia(PHONE).matches; } catch (e) { return false; }
  }
  function stripHeight() {
    var s = doc.querySelector(".toptabs");
    return s ? Math.round(s.getBoundingClientRect().height) : 0;
  }

  /* ── the summary line ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     One reading per .fgroup, in the panel's own order. A select contributes
     its selected option's text ("t-SNE"); anything with a numeric value
     contributes "<short label> <value>" ("perplexity 30"). The short label is
     the LAST word of the group's own <label>, which is what makes the output
     read like the owner's example without any per-demo table: "t-SNE
     perplexity" -> "perplexity", "K-means clusters k" -> "k".

     A DISABLED control is skipped, and that is a feature rather than an
     omission: tbb disables "UMAP n_neighbors" while t-SNE is selected, so the
     summary names only the parameters actually in force — which is exactly the
     owner's "t-SNE · perplexity 30 · k 6", with n_neighbors absent. */
  function shortLabel(group) {
    var lab = group.querySelector("label");
    var t = lab && lab.textContent ? lab.textContent.trim() : "";
    if (!t) return "";
    t = t.replace(/[:：]\s*$/, "");
    var words = t.split(/\s+/);
    return words[words.length - 1];
  }
  function controlOf(group) {
    return group.querySelector(
      'select,input[type="range"],input[type="number"],input[type="checkbox"],input[type="radio"]');
  }
  function readingFor(group) {
    var c = controlOf(group);
    if (!c || c.disabled || c.getAttribute("aria-disabled") === "true") return "";
    if (c.tagName === "SELECT") {
      var o = c.options[c.selectedIndex];
      var t = o && o.textContent ? o.textContent.trim() : "";
      if (!t) return "";
      /* A "— pick a held-out material —" placeholder is a prompt, not a value,
         and it crowds out the readings that are. Skipped while it is the
         selection; the moment a real option is chosen it appears. */
      if (/^[—–-]/.test(t) && /[—–-]$/.test(t)) return "";
      /* A select whose options are bare numbers says nothing on its own — tbb's
         perplexity select reads "30", which could be anything. When the option
         text carries no letter, prefix the group's short label, so the summary
         reads "perplexity 30" beside a self-describing "t-SNE". */
      if (!/[A-Za-z]/.test(t)) {
        var s = shortLabel(group);
        return s ? s + " " + t : t;
      }
      return t;
    }
    if (c.type === "checkbox" || c.type === "radio") {
      return c.checked ? shortLabel(group) : "";
    }
    var v = String(c.value == null ? "" : c.value).trim();
    if (v === "") return "";
    var s = shortLabel(group);
    return s ? s + " " + v : v;
  }
  function summarize(panel) {
    var groups = panel.querySelectorAll(".fgroup");
    var parts = [];
    if (groups.length) {
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(groups, function (g) {
        var r = readingFor(g);
        if (r) parts.push(r);
      });
    } else {
      /* a panel that never adopted .fgroup: fall back to the bare controls */
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(
        panel.querySelectorAll('select,input[type="range"]'), function (c) {
          if (c.disabled) return;
          if (c.tagName === "SELECT") {
            var o = c.options[c.selectedIndex];
            if (o && o.textContent) parts.push(o.textContent.trim());
          } else if (c.value != null && String(c.value) !== "") {
            parts.push(String(c.value));
          }
        });
    }
    return parts.join(" · ");
  }

  /* ── one bar per panel ───────────────────────────────────────────────────*/
  var SEQ = 0;

  function enhance(panel) {
    if (!panel || panel.__pcParamBar) return null;
    if (!panel.parentNode) return null;

    if (!panel.id) panel.id = "pcFilters" + (++SEQ);

    var bar = doc.createElement("div");
    bar.className = "parambar";

    var btn = doc.createElement("button");
    btn.type = "button";                       // never a submit inside a form
    btn.className = "parambar-btn";
    btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    btn.setAttribute("aria-controls", panel.id);

    var key = doc.createElement("span");
    key.className = "parambar-k";
    key.textContent = "Parameters";

    var sum = doc.createElement("span");
    sum.className = "parambar-sum";

    var chev = doc.createElement("span");
    chev.className = "parambar-chev";
    chev.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
    chev.textContent = "▾";               // ▾ — the same glyph base.css uses

    btn.appendChild(key);
    btn.appendChild(sum);
    btn.appendChild(chev);
    bar.appendChild(btn);
    panel.parentNode.insertBefore(bar, panel);
    /* The panel moves INSIDE the bar, and the phone stylesheet then drops it
       out of flow as a dropdown anchored to the bar (position:absolute against
       the sticky bar). That is what makes the expansion deterministic: an
       inline push-down opens at the bar's NATURAL position, so once the bar is
       pinned the panel appears off-screen above it, and Chrome's scroll
       anchoring then shifts scrollY by the panel's own height to hold the
       visual position — re-hiding what the tap just revealed (measured twice:
       scrollY 902 -> 1264). Anchored to the pinned bar there is no scroll maths
       to get wrong and nothing for anchoring to fight.

       Off the phone the bar is display:contents, so this nesting is invisible:
       .filters renders in the panel's flow exactly where it always did. */
    bar.appendChild(panel);

    var inst = { panel: panel, bar: bar, btn: btn, sum: sum, chev: chev, open: false };
    panel.__pcParamBar = inst;

    function refresh() {
      var text = summarize(panel);
      sum.textContent = text;
      btn.setAttribute("aria-label",
        (inst.open ? "Hide" : "Show") + " analysis parameters" + (text ? " — " + text : ""));
    }

    function setOpen(open) {
      inst.open = !!open;
      panel.setAttribute("data-pc-param", open ? "open" : "collapsed");
      btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", open ? "true" : "false");
      chev.textContent = open ? "▸" : "▾";      // ▸ closes / ▾ opens
      refresh();
      /* No scrolling on open. The panel is a DROPDOWN anchored to the bar,
         so wherever the bar is — pinned under the tab strip or still in the
         flow — the panel opens directly beneath it and is already on screen.
         The earlier inline push-down needed a scroll correction and lost a
         race with Chrome's scroll anchoring twice (scrollY 902 -> 1264, the
         panel's own height); anchoring the panel to the bar removes the
         problem rather than compensating for it. */
    }

    btn.addEventListener("click", function () { setOpen(!inst.open); });

    /* A committed value collapses the panel so the plot it just changed is on
       screen. `change`, not `input`: a range fires `input` continuously while
       the thumb is moving, and collapsing mid-drag would take the control out
       from under the finger. So dragging keeps live feedback through `input`
       (summary only) and commits on release through `change`. */
    panel.addEventListener("input", function () { refresh(); });
    panel.addEventListener("change", function () {
      refresh();
      if (isPhone() && inst.open) setOpen(false);
    });

    inst.refresh = refresh;
    inst.setOpen = setOpen;
    setOpen(false);
    return inst;
  }

  /* Only the FIRST .filters inside a given panel becomes a bar. Two sticky
     bars in one view would pin at the same offset and overlap; a second
     control panel in the same tab is left alone and logged for phase 2. */
  function install() {
    var seen = {};
    var panels = doc.querySelectorAll(".filters");
    for (var i = 0; i < panels.length; i++) {
      var p = panels[i];
      var host = p.closest ? (p.closest(".toppanel") || doc.body) : doc.body;
      var key = host.id || "body";
      if (seen[key]) continue;                 // one bar per view
      seen[key] = true;
      enhance(p);
    }
    position();
    sync();
  }

  /* The sticky offset is the LIVE tab-strip height (DESIGN.md §5.2), not a
     constant: the strip is 46px on a phone and 67px on a laptop, and it
     changes when the chips reflow. */
  function position() {
    var h = stripHeight();
    var bars = doc.querySelectorAll(".parambar");
    for (var i = 0; i < bars.length; i++) bars[i].style.top = h + "px";
  }

  /* Off the phone the panel must be exactly what it always was: no data-attr,
     so no CSS from §23C applies and .filters keeps its own sticky rule. */
  function sync() {
    var phone = isPhone();
    var panels = doc.querySelectorAll(".filters");
    for (var i = 0; i < panels.length; i++) {
      var p = panels[i], inst = p.__pcParamBar;
      if (!inst) continue;
      if (phone) {
        if (!p.hasAttribute("data-pc-param")) inst.setOpen(false);
        else inst.refresh();
      } else {
        p.removeAttribute("data-pc-param");
        inst.open = false;
        inst.btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
      }
    }
    position();
  }

  function boot() {
    install();
    setTimeout(install, 0);
    global.addEventListener("load", function () { setTimeout(install, 0); });
    global.addEventListener("resize", function () { sync(); });
    /* the strip's height changes when a tab is selected, and a newly shown
       panel's bar has never been positioned */
    doc.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      if (e.target && e.target.closest && e.target.closest(".toptabs")) {
        (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(function () {
          install();
        });
      }
    }, false);
    try {
      var mq = global.matchMedia(PHONE);
      if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener("change", sync);
      else if (mq.addListener) mq.addListener(sync);
    } catch (e) {}
  }

  if (doc.readyState === "loading") doc.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", boot);
  else boot();

  if (global.PC) {
    global.PC.installParamBars = install;
    global.PC.syncParamBars = sync;
  }
})(typeof globalThis !== "undefined" ? globalThis : this);

/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   PHONE CHART OVERLAY  —  page behaviour module
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   A chart panel on a phone is ~330px wide whatever it draws, and most of them
   are shorter than they are wide, so the plot the reader came for is a strip.
   This gives every plot an expand affordance at phone width: tap it and the
   panel covers the viewport; rotate and the chart redraws with the whole
   landscape width; tap ✕ or press Escape and it goes back.

   HOW IT REDRAWS — the one mechanism that needs no per-demo cooperation.
   Every demo template binds `window` `resize` to its own redraw (verified: all
   8 templates, exactly one listener each) and every draw function sizes itself
   from `cv.parentNode.clientWidth`. So the overlay changes the panel's width
   and dispatches a synthetic `resize`; each demo redraws itself, at its own
   aspect logic, through the code path it already uses for a window resize.
   Nothing here knows or assumes what any panel draws — which is also why a
   keep-ratio panel stays honest: tbb's map computes h = w × GEO.aspect, so it
   letterboxes itself at any width the overlay gives it.

   NO DOM MOVE — a considered deviation from the brief's "move the live panel
   node". The node is never reparented: the panel is promoted IN PLACE with
   position:fixed. Moving it out of its .toppanel would take it out of the
   subtree every demo's redraw scopes to (`.toppanel:not([hidden])`), so the
   panel would stop being redrawn — the exact failure the brief's "not a clone"
   instruction exists to prevent. Promoting in place satisfies that intent more
   strongly: it IS the live node, still inside its panel, still found by the
   demo's own selectors, with its listeners and PC.hover binding untouched.

   Z-ORDER: 90 — above the sticky tab strip (30) and the parameter bar (25),
   below #tip (100) so a tooltip still paints over a full-screen chart.
   ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
(function (global) {
  "use strict";
  var doc = global.document;
  if (!doc) return;

  /* Width OR height — see components.css §23D. A phone in landscape is 844x390:
     a width-only test calls that "desktop" and tears the overlay down at the
     moment rotation is supposed to help (measured: zoomOpen true -> false on
     rotate). The max-width:950px bound keeps a short desktop window out. */
  var PHONE = "(max-width: 640px), (max-height: 640px) and (max-width: 950px)";
  function isPhone() {
    try { return global.matchMedia(PHONE).matches; } catch (e) { return false; }
  }

  /* The wrappers demos actually put a plot in. First match wins; a canvas with
     none of them falls back to its own parent. */
  var BOXES = ".pbox,.chartbox,.plotwrap,.bookbox,.plot-card,.dm,.mxcard,.scard";
  var open = null;                          // the promoted box, or null

  /* ONE box-detection for the whole suite. PC.plotBoxOf (the touch-mode block
     in the core library) holds the same selector list and is what the docked
     readout and the selection ring use; delegating to it is what guarantees
     the ⤢ button, the readout and the ring land in the same container — and
     therefore that all three survive this overlay promoting that container.
     The local copy stays as the fallback for a page that somehow loads this
     module without the core. */
  function boxFor(cv) {
    var PC = global.PC;
    if (PC && typeof PC.plotBoxOf === "function") return PC.plotBoxOf(cv);
    var b = cv.closest ? cv.closest(BOXES) : null;
    return b || cv.parentElement;
  }

  function plotCanvases() {
    var out = [], all = doc.querySelectorAll("canvas");
    for (var i = 0; i < all.length; i++) {
      var c = all[i];
      if (c.classList.contains("storycanvas")) continue;      // §2.4 thumbnails
      if (c.getAttribute("aria-hidden") === "true") continue;
      out.push(c);
    }
    return out;
  }

  /* PC.fit() writes cv.style.width, and the measure-the-box call signature
     (PC.fit(cv) / PC.fit(cv, null, h)) then re-measures the canvas's OWN frozen
     inline width instead of the container's — so once a canvas has been fitted
     it can never grow again. Measured on pleiades with the overlay open in
     landscape: inline width 337px inside a 365px box, and the chart stayed
     337px however wide the overlay got.
     Clearing the inline WIDTH (never the height — demos that pass an explicit h
     depend on it, and a cleared height would collapse a canvas with no CSS
     height to PC.fit's 160px floor) lets the next fit read the real container.
     A demo that passes explicit w/h simply writes both again and is unaffected. */
  function unfreeze(box) {
    if (!box) return;
    var cvs = box.querySelectorAll("canvas");
    for (var i = 0; i < cvs.length; i++) {
      if (cvs[i].classList.contains("storycanvas")) continue;
      cvs[i].style.width = "";
    }
  }

  /* Every demo redraws on window resize; that is the hook. rAF first, so the
     promoted box has been laid out at its new width before anything measures. */
  function redraw() {
    (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(function () {
      var ev;
      try { ev = new Event("resize"); }
      catch (e) { ev = doc.createEvent("Event"); ev.initEvent("resize", true, true); }
      global.dispatchEvent(ev);
    });
  }

  function chromeOf(box) {
    var kids = box.children;
    for (var i = 0; i < kids.length; i++) {
      if (kids[i].className === "pczoom-chrome") return kids[i];
    }
    return null;
  }
  function btnOf(box) {
    var kids = box.children;
    for (var i = 0; i < kids.length; i++) {
      if (kids[i].className === "pczoom-btn") return kids[i];
    }
    return null;
  }

  function closeZoom() {
    if (!open) return;
    var box = open;
    open = null;
    box.classList.remove("pczoom-on");
    var chrome = chromeOf(box);
    if (chrome) chrome.parentNode.removeChild(chrome);
    doc.documentElement.classList.remove("pczoom-lock");
    var btn = btnOf(box);
    if (btn) btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    try { if (global.PC && global.PC.hideTip) global.PC.hideTip(); } catch (e) {}
    unfreeze(box);
    redraw();
    if (btn) { try { btn.focus(); } catch (e) {} }
  }

  function openZoom(box) {
    if (open) closeZoom();
    open = box;
    box.classList.add("pczoom-on");
    doc.documentElement.classList.add("pczoom-lock");
    var btn = btnOf(box);
    if (btn) btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");

    var chrome = doc.createElement("div");
    chrome.className = "pczoom-chrome";

    /* One line, and it takes itself away. Permanent chrome would compete with
       the chart the reader just asked to look at. */
    var hint = doc.createElement("p");
    hint.className = "pczoom-hint";
    hint.textContent = "Rotate for a wider view";
    setTimeout(function () { hint.className = "pczoom-hint gone"; }, 3200);

    var close = doc.createElement("button");
    close.type = "button";
    close.className = "pczoom-close";
    close.setAttribute("aria-label", "Close full-screen chart");
    close.textContent = "✕";
    close.addEventListener("click", function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); closeZoom(); });

    chrome.appendChild(hint);
    chrome.appendChild(close);
    box.insertBefore(chrome, box.firstChild);

    try { if (global.PC && global.PC.hideTip) global.PC.hideTip(); } catch (e) {}
    unfreeze(box);
    redraw();
    try { close.focus(); } catch (e) {}
  }

  function enhance(box) {
    if (!box || box.__pcZoom) return;
    box.__pcZoom = true;
    box.classList.add("pczoom-host");

    var btn = doc.createElement("button");
    btn.type = "button";
    btn.className = "pczoom-btn";
    btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    btn.setAttribute("aria-label", "View this chart full screen");
    btn.textContent = "⤢";              // ⤢ expand, a real glyph (§1.5)
    btn.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      e.preventDefault();
      e.stopPropagation();
      if (open === box) closeZoom(); else openZoom(box);
    });
    box.appendChild(btn);
  }

  function install() {
    var cvs = plotCanvases();
    for (var i = 0; i < cvs.length; i++) {
      var box = boxFor(cvs[i]);
      if (!box) continue;
      /* A demo opts a panel out by marking it, for anything the overlay is
         MEASURED to break. Nothing is opted out at the time of writing. */
      if (box.getAttribute && box.getAttribute("data-pc-zoom") === "off") continue;
      enhance(box);
    }
  }

  function boot() {
    install();
    setTimeout(install, 0);
    global.addEventListener("load", function () { setTimeout(install, 0); });

    /* a newly shown tab holds panels that have never been enhanced */
    doc.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
      if (e.target && e.target.closest && e.target.closest(".toptabs")) {
        (global.requestAnimationFrame || function (f) { return setTimeout(f, 16); })(install);
      }
    }, false);

    /* Rotation fires a real resize. The promoted box is now a different width,
       so the same unfreeze has to happen before the demo re-fits — otherwise the
       chart keeps the width it was frozen at when the overlay opened. */
    global.addEventListener("resize", function () {
      if (!open) return;
      unfreeze(open);
    });

    doc.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
      if (open && (e.key === "Escape" || e.key === "Esc")) {
        e.preventDefault();
        closeZoom();
      }
    });

    /* Leaving phone width with a panel promoted would strand it: the §23D rules
       stop applying and the box would keep its chrome. */
    try {
      var mq = global.matchMedia(PHONE);
      var onChange = function () { if (!isPhone()) closeZoom(); };
      if (mq.addEventListener) mq.addEventListener("change", onChange);
      else if (mq.addListener) mq.addListener(onChange);
    } catch (e) {}
  }

  if (doc.readyState === "loading") doc.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", boot);
  else boot();

  if (global.PC) {
    global.PC.installChartZoom = install;
    global.PC.closeChartZoom = closeZoom;
    global.PC.zoomOpen = function () { return !!open; };
  }
})(typeof globalThis !== "undefined" ? globalThis : this);
